papers.title: Analytic Criteria for Detecting Bernstein-Sato Roots
papers.abstract: We study roots of Bernstein-Sato polynomials of ideals. Our first main result gives a general partial differential equation criterion for detecting roots of the Bernstein-Sato polynomial of an ideal. For homogeneous case, we recast this criterion as an analytic condition, connecting the algebraic problem of locating roots with analytic properties of the defining data. As an application, we give a series of roots for the general determinantal ideal prove the strong monodromy conjecture for them. Keywords. Bernstein-Sato polynomial, determinantal variety, monodromy conjecture.

papers.title: Gauss-Manin Connection in Disguise: Holomorphic Anomaly Equations and Higher Genus Real Gromov-Witten Invariants
papers.abstract: We construct an algebraic framework for the extended holomorphic anomaly equations following ideas of Alim, Movasati, Scheidegger and Yau. We choose the quintic threefold as our main model and use this framework to solve the equations and fix the ambiguity up to genus 5. We obtain predictions for real Gromov-Witten invariants, or, equivalently, real Gopakumar-Vafa invariants that are integers and agree with their complex counterparts modulo 2. In the end, we discuss how the framework could be extended and compute the same predictions for the bicubic up to genus 9.

papers.title: A Functorial Classification of Toric Stacks
papers.abstract: Toric stacks enrich the study of toric varieties by accounting for quotients of actions of diagonalizable groups. In practice, toric stacks are constructed and understood via "stacky fans" generalizing the fans appearing in toric geometry. Previous attempts to make this construction into an equivalence of categories have either run into crucial errors or have been restricted to special cases (e.g. only considering separated Deligne-Mumford stacks). In this paper, we solve this problem by introducing a new 2-category $\mathsf{StkFan}$ of stacky fans and constructing an equivalence of 2-categories between $\mathsf{StkFan}$ and a 2-category $\mathsf{TStk}$ of toric stacks. Along the way, we develop a theory of "toric categories" which categorifies the classical theory of toric monoids. We also explain how working with toric categories provides a simple axiomatic framework for Gale duality.

papers.title: Dynamical degrees of automorphisms of non-projective hyperk\"ahler manifolds
papers.abstract: We determine the dynamical degrees of bimeromorphic automorphisms of hyperk\"ahler manifolds of all known deformation types with irreducible characteristic polynomial.

papers.title: Stability of vector bundles and reduction mod $p$
papers.abstract: Let $E$ be a vector bundle on a normal complex projective variety. We prove that slope stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ and Zariski density of the reductions of $E$ modulo $p$ that are not strongly geometrically stable imply that the bundle $E$ is projectively unitary flat. This generalizes Shepherd--Barron's result from rank $2$ to arbitrary rank. We also show that if $E$ has rank $\le 3$ we can replace stability of $\mathop{Sym}^2E$ by stability of $E$ but we cannot do so if $E$ has rank $4$. We also generalize these results to reflexive sheaves on some mildly singular normal complex projective varieties.

papers.title: The fifteenth cohomology group of moduli spaces of stable curves
papers.abstract: The new framework of semi-tautological extensions has allowed for explicit understanding of low-degree odd cohomology groups of moduli spaces of stable curves. Let $S^*_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) \subset H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ denote the semi-tautological extension generated by $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$, that is, the smallest system of subrings of $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ containing $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,11})$ and the tautological subrings, which is also closed under pullbacks along forgetful maps and pushforwards along gluing maps. Recently, it has been shown that $H^{11}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{11}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ and $H^{13}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = S^{13}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g$ and $n$. Meanwhile, $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n}) \neq S_\omega^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{1,n})$ for all $n \geq 15$. Nevertheless, we prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n}) = S^{15}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{2,n})$ for all $n$. Moreover, we determine all relations in $S_\omega^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for all $g \geq 2$ and give explicit bases for this vector space in terms of decorated graphs. Conditional upon the conjectured dimension of $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,14})$, we also prove that $H^{15}(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n}) = S^{15}_\omega(\overline{\mathcal M}_{3,n})$ for all $n$. As an application, we prove $H^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n}) = RH^*(\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,n})$ for several new small pairs $(g,n)$.

papers.title: The canonical class and Chern character operators on Hilbert schemes of points
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth projective complex surface. We obtain explicit formulas for the Chern character operators on the Hilbert schemes of points $X^{[n]}$ in terms of Nakajima operators, determining in particular the coefficients of the terms involving the canonical class $K_X$ and its square. Consequently, the cohomology ring structure of the Hilbert scheme is determined. As an application, we give an alternative proof of the action of the affine Yangian $Y_{t_1,t_2}(\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_1)$ on the cohomological Fock space $\mathbb{H}_X = \bigoplus_{n\geq 0} H^*(X^{[n]},\mathbb{Q})$.

papers.title: Characterization of $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of small rank
papers.abstract: The $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a polynomial map is a quadratic enrichment of the classical Milnor number, defined as the local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree of the gradient. We study which elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of nondegenerate symmetric bilinear forms arise as $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers. Over fields of characteristic not $2$, $3$, or $5$, we show that every element of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $7$ that is a local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degree is also an $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number. Unlike for local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees, however, in general not all $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers can be obtained from two-variable polynomials. Over an arbitrary field of characteristic not $2$, $3$, $5$, or $7$, we characterize the elements of the Grothendieck-Witt ring of rank at most $8$ that are $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor numbers of two-variable polynomials. Over subfields of $\mathbb{R}$, this implies that there are local $\mathbb{A}^1$-Brouwer degrees of ranks $4$, $6$, and $8$ that are not the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number of a two-variable polynomial. We also prove that under a mild hypothesis one can reduce the number of variables of a polynomial while preserving the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Milnor number up to multiplication by a unit.

papers.title: A degree-linear upper bound for the P\'olya exponent of forms with fixed arity
papers.abstract: Let $P = \sum_{\omega} a_\omega x^\omega$ be a degree $d$ homogeneous polynomial in $x_0, \dots, x_n$ with real coefficients. P\'olya showed that, if $P$ is strictly positive on the standard $n$-simplex, then $(x_0 + \cdots + x_n)^M P$ has strictly positive coefficients for all $M \gg 0$. The least such $M$ is known as the \emph{P\'olya exponent} of $P$. de Klerk-Laurent-Parrilo showed that the P\'olya exponent is $O(d^2) P^{(0)}_{\max}/\lambda(P)$, where $P^{(0)}_{\max} := \max_\omega a_\omega/\binom{d}{\omega}$ and $\lambda(P)$ is the infimum of $P$ on the standard simplex. P\'olya's Positivstellensatz is a consequence of the classical approximation of the multivariate hypergeometric distribution by the multinomial distribution, as was already implicitly known to de Klerk-Laurent-Sun. By applying known estimates of this approximation from probability theory, we obtain a different $O_n(d) L(P)/\lambda(P)$ upper bound of the P\'olya exponent, where $L(P) := \max |a_\omega|/\binom{d}{\omega}$. An example shows that $O_n(d)$ is tight.

papers.title: Cetraro lectures on integrable systems and moduli spaces of curves
papers.abstract: In these lecture notes we review some constructions and results on the relation between topology of the moduli space of stable curves and integrable systems of evolutionary PDEs.

papers.title: Affine realization of tilted Richardson varieties
papers.abstract: Richardson varieties provide geometric representatives for products of Schubert classes, with stratifications indexed by the subintervals of Bruhat intervals. We construct analogous geometric models for tilted Bruhat intervals for all split connected reductive groups. Our construction uses Richardson varieties in affine flag varieties and yields abstract tilted Richardson varieties whose isomorphism classes, together with their labeled stratifications, are independent of the choices involved. We obtain an explicit formula for the point-counting polynomials of their open parts in terms of increasing minimal weight paths, extending Dyer's formula for Kazhdan--Lusztig $R$-polynomials. Over the real numbers, their totally nonnegative parts are regular CW complexes homeomorphic to closed balls, which gives a natural geometric realization of the posets of tilted Bruhat subintervals in all Lie types. Over the complex numbers, we prove that their fundamental classes push forward under a continuous loop evaluation map to the Poincar\'e duals of the minimal-degree coefficients of quantum Schubert products.

papers.title: On Chow and Picard groups of Richardson varieties
papers.abstract: We show that if $\Pi \subseteq G/P$ is a projected Richardson variety, then the degree map $\mathrm{Pic}(\Pi) \to A_1(\Pi)^\vee$ is injective. Moreover, it is an isomorphism in characteristic zero and in all but finitely many positive characteristics. We conjecture that it is an isomorphism in every characteristic. Our proofs are geometric, using a linear paving, topological properties of klt singularities, and reduction to characteristic zero.

papers.title: Some Remarks on Regular Sequences and Complete Intersections
papers.abstract: We give an ideal in a polynomial ring in three variables, generated by three elements and having height equal to three, but for which no permutation of its generators is a regular sequence. We prove that in a polynomial ring over an infinite field, an ideal of height n generated by n polynomials, always admits a set of n generators, for which any permutation is a regular sequence.

papers.title: The a-number of the Serre-type maximal curves of Abd\'on-Bezerra-Quoos
papers.abstract: For every prime power $q$, we determine the $a$-number of the Serre-type maximal curves $X(q,n)$: $y^{q^2}-y=x^{(q^n+1)/(q+1)}$ over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$, $n\ge 3$ odd, introduced by Abd\'on, Bezerra and Quoos as a generalization of Serre's curve $y^4+y=x^3$ over $\mathbb{F}_{64}$. The Weierstrass semigroup at the unique point at infinity gives an explicit basis of holomorphic differentials, on which the Cartier operator acts by monomials; this reduces the $a$-number to a lattice-point count, which we evaluate in closed form.

papers.title: A note on stability conditions on product-quotient surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a product-quotient surface, which is by definition a minimal resolution of $(C_1\times C_2)/G$, where $C_i$ are smooth curves of genus $\geq 2$ and $G$ is a finite group. When $G$ acts freely, we show that every product Bridgeland stability condition on $C_1\times C_2$ induces a tilt stability condition on $X$, and that, if $p_g(X)=q(X)=0$, every tilt stability condition on $X$ arises this way. When $(C_1\times C_2)/G$ has only $A_1$-singularities, we use induction \cite{MMS} and derived McKay correspondence \cite{BKR} to produce non-geometric stability conditions $\sigma_X$ on $X$, which satisfy the full support property and lie in the closure of the geometric chamber. Whether $\sigma_X$ also lies in the closure of the $\widetilde{\mathrm{GL}}^+(2,\mathbb{R})$-orbit of the tilt stability conditions depends on a single inequality, $\omega_X^2 \ge n/8$, where $n$ is the number of $A_1$-singularities. When it fails, the geometric chamber is strictly larger than this orbit.

papers.title: Spectral G\aa rding Elliptic Equations
papers.abstract: We study spectral G\aa rding elliptic equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal G\aa rding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Sz\'ekelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact K\"ahler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal G\aa rding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.

papers.title: Rationality of Kontsevich moduli of stable maps, and their Galois descents
papers.abstract: Let k be a field and X be a geometrically rational variety over k. We investigate the Kontsevich moduli spaces of genus zero, stable maps with curve classes of low degree on X over k, and define their twisted Galois descents. We study the k-rationality of these spaces in detail when X is a projective space/Severi Brauer variety and when X is moduli of genus zero n-marked points. When X is a homogeneous variety over the field of complex numbers, this is a well-known theorem of Kim-Pandharipande.

papers.title: Crystals and the parabolicity conjecture
papers.abstract: These notes introduce crystals and crystalline Dieudonn\'e theory through the example of abelian varieties. After discussing $p$-divisible groups, $F$-isocrystals, slope filtrations, and overconvergence, we explain the parabolicity theorem for $F$-isocrystals and some of its applications to monodromy and Hecke orbits. Two appendices formulate research projects on isocrystals over formal schemes and on monodromy beyond the constant-slope setting. The exposition is intended for readers familiar with basic algebraic geometry and the \'etale and fppf topologies; prior knowledge of Witt vectors is helpful but not required.

papers.title: Topological Classification of Univariate Sparse Polynomials via Tropical Geometry
papers.abstract: We give the topological classification of some simplest univariate complex fewnomials, and find tropical fans of the fewnomial strata with each topological type. Specifically, for the support $ A=\{d,d+1,d+2,d+3,d+4\},\quad d\geq3, $ we classify the topological equivalence classes of polynomials having two critical values of ramification type $(2,2)$. There is one class for odd $d$ and two classes for even $d$. We describe the branches at infinity of the corresponding one-dimensional stratum using Newton polytopes of certain complete intersection representations of the sought strata, and determine their tropicalizations. The combinatorial types of the obtained tropical polynomials distinguishes all three kinds of topological equivalence classes. These computations suggest a correspondence between topological equivalence classes of polynomials and combinatorial types of tropicalizations of their branches at infinity, as well as a possible periodicity phenomenon under translations of the support.

papers.title: Beyond Amoeba Boundaries
papers.abstract: We construct smooth plane curves whose logarithmic contours are smooth and embedded but strictly larger than their amoeba boundaries. The examples include connected irreducible curves, disconnected unions of nonlinear components with two-dimensional amoebas, nested families with arbitrarily many components, and a uniform construction realizing every positive genus. Exact critical-locus calculations distinguish the boundary-producing folds from compact or noncompact contour branches lying in the amoeba interior. These constructions show that smoothness of the complete contour does not force contour--boundary equality and that internal critical-value branches persist under monomial transformations, controlled perturbations, and finite monomial coverings.21 pages, 14 figures

papers.title: Beyond Harnack Amoeba Boundaries
papers.abstract: We construct smooth irreducible plane curves whose complete amoeba contour is a smooth embedded curve equal to the amoeba boundary, although the curves are not torically equivalent to simple Harnack curves. Finite monomial coverings yield explicit infinite families with higher logarithmic multiplicity and nonmaximal normalized amoeba area. We classify the Newton polygons admitting such covering constructions through their exponent lattices, give an exact connectedness criterion in terms of monodromy, and treat primitive polygons by a separate phase-sensitive construction. Exact triangular and trapezoidal families are complemented by positive-genus investigations exhibiting bounded amoeba-complement components. These results show that a perfectly exposed amoeba contour does not determine the real structure, logarithmic sheet number, or Harnack type of the underlying curve.

papers.title: Post-critically finite polynomials in characteristic $p$
papers.abstract: It follows from the compactness of the connectedness locus that the locus of PCF polynomials in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d (at least 2) over the complex number is a countable union of zero-dimensional subvarieties. Over fields of characteristic p the analogous claim is certainly false, so it is natural to ask how large the components of the PCF locus can be. We show that the components of the PCF locus in the moduli space of polynomials of degree d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 have dimension at most d/p and that this bound is sharp, in the strong sense that for every p and d there are infinitely many distinct PCF components whose dimension is the greatest integer no greater than this bound (except in the case $p=d=2$).

papers.title: Total Cohomology of Hilbert schemes of Orbisurfaces I: Reduction to Stacky Loci
papers.abstract: We generalize Nakajima's theory of Hilbert schemes of points on surfaces to Hilbert schemes of points on \textit{orbisurfaces}, and obtain initial factorization based on stratification by stabilizers. While the usual formula is retained for the trivial stabilizer stratum and for those strata of codimension $1$, genuine difficulties arise with stacky points strata. In the local picture of an isolated stacky point, the theory reduce to the study of $\Quot^\bfv[\CC^2/G]$ for a \textit{small} finite subgroup of $GL_2(\CC)$. The generating series for their total cohomology is a geometric correction of the generating series for total cohomology of ordinary smooth surface schemes. In addition, we obtain an action of the Borel-Moore homology of the punctual fibre stacks on the total Hilbert cohomology by virtual correspondences, in analogy with the Fock space description in Nakajima's theory. The punctual fibre stacks are genuinely different from the symmetric stack, and has natural realizations via motivic integration.

papers.title: A Sharp Bound for the Second Betti Number of Hyperk\"ahler Sixfolds
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth compact irreducible hyperk\"ahler manifold of dimension six. We prove that the second Betti number satisfies $b_2(X) \le 23$. Furthermore, we show that the third cohomology vanishes whenever $b_2(X) \ge 19$, and that all odd cohomology vanishes when $b_2(X) = 23$. If the second Chern class lies in the subalgebra generated by $H^2(X,\mathbb{Q})$, then $b_2(X) \in \{5,8,23\}$. The proof uses the Looijenga--Lunts--Verbitsky decomposition, curvature inequalities for Segre classes, and the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations on the projective cotangent bundle.

papers.title: Open substacks preserving moduli spaces: classification and bounds
papers.abstract: For a smooth locally reductive stack admitting an adequate moduli space, we show that there are finitely many open substacks preserving the adequate moduli space, and give a complete classification of such opens. For $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions, this becomes an explicit description in terms of the codimension-one Bialynicki-Birula strata. Moreover, for a stable adequate moduli space, we show that the number of preserving opens are bounded by 3 raised to the relative Picard rank. As an application, the number of fixed components for $\mathbb{G}_m$-actions is at least the relative Picard rank.

papers.title: Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and the real Nullstellensatz for modules and sheaves
papers.abstract: We prove the geometric halves of Hilbert's Nullstellensatz and of the real Nullstellensatz for submodules of finitely generated modules and for coherent sheaves, complementing our earlier result that semiprime (resp. real) submodules are intersections of prime (resp. real prime) submodules. First, we pass from prime to maximal submodules: over a Jacobson ring, a prime submodule $P$ of $M$ is an intersection of maximal submodules whenever $M/P$ is a torsionless $R/(P:M)$-module, in particular whenever $M/P$ is finitely generated (the latter case is due to Maani Shirazi and Sharif). Consequently, if $R$ is a finitely generated algebra over an algebraically closed field and $M$ is finitely generated, the smallest semiprime submodule containing a submodule $N$ of $M$ consists of all $f\in M$ such that, for every point $a$, the value $f(a)$ (i.e. the image of $f$ in the fibre $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$) lies in $N(a)$ (i.e. the image of $N$ in $M/\mathfrak{m}_aM$). We prove the real analogues over real Jacobson rings; for finitely generated algebras over a real closed field they are determined by the real points. The module classifications and directional vanishing formulas yield both Nullstellens\"atze for coherent sheaves on schemes of finite type over a field. We also prove compatibility of semiprimeness, reality and both radicals with arbitrary localization, and the resulting stalk criteria.

papers.title: The moduli space of cubic surfaces and its orbifold fundamental group
papers.abstract: We find a new presentation of the orbifold fundamental group of the moduli space of cubic surfaces, based on the Artin group of the Petersen graph. This group has two well-known quotients, which appear in the simplest possible way: killing the squares resp. sixth powers of our generators yields the Coxeter group $W(E_6)$ resp. a certain arithmetic group in $\operatorname{PU}(1,4)$. Along the way we present a certain central extension by $\mathbb{Z}$, of the genus zero mapping class group with any number of punctures. The $6$-puncture case is essential in this paper, and the general case may have independent interest.

papers.title: Stein degree over fields of characteristic zero
papers.abstract: We show that the Stein degree of horizontal divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations or certain vertical divisors of Fano type fibrations over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero is bounded by constants that are independent on the ground field.

papers.title: Mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes
papers.abstract: This work studies the relationship between the multigrading in the cohomology of moment-angle complexes, introduced by V. Buchstaber and T. Panov in their computation of these cohomology groups, and the multigrading in the cohomology of the corresponding complements of coordinate subspace arrangements, arising from the mixed Hodge structure. It is shown that these multigradings coincide. This result refines a theorem from Yu. Eliyashev's 2013 dissertation. Furthermore, results on the mixed Hodge structure in the cohomology of complements of coordinate subspace arrangements are applied to the study of the same varieties over finite fields. In particular, various formulas are obtained for the number of $\mathbb{F}_q$-rational points and for the associated global $\zeta$-functions.

papers.title: Logarithmic Kunz and Radu--Andr\'e Theorems
papers.abstract: Frobenius morphisms play a crucial role in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra in positive characteristic. In particular, \textit{the Kunz theorem}, characterizing non-singularity via Frobenius morphisms, is a monumental work and has a relative version, called \textit{the Radu--Andr\'e theorem}. In this paper, we extend the Kunz theorem and the Radu--Andr\'e theorem to logarithmic algebraic geometry in positive characteristic.
